title: Channel muting decisions
intro: Four things wait on you before channel muting can be built: one open question in the doc, the toggle copy, a limit, and one step only you can run. Each one says why it is asked, what waits on it and what happens if you leave it.

words.badge: The red number on the app icon that counts unread messages.
words.push: A notification that shows on the phone's lock screen.

items.plain: When a member mutes a channel, should its threads go quiet too?
items.why: The doc says muting ships without thread-level muting, but its **How we'll know** signal says Ana gets zero notifications from the channel for a day. Thread replies notify today, so the doc as written can fail its own signal.
items.blocks: §5 Mechanism (which notifier reads the mute table) and a fourth acceptance row, if threads are included. Phase 1 of the build can start either way.
items.ifNoAnswer: The doc ships as written: threads keep notifying, and the signal is checked only in channels with no threads.
items.example: Ana mutes #general at 09:00. At 11:00 Ben replies in a thread Ana started last week. With threads muted, Ana gets nothing. Without, she gets a push from a channel she muted.

evidence.note: the signal: zero notifications from the channel for a day
every channel member is notified on every message (`messages.ts:88`); thread replies take the same path
the question as the doc asks it

options.label: Muting a channel also mutes its threads
options.because: it is the only answer under which the doc's own signal holds for every channel.
options.commits: one mute check read by both the channel and the thread notifier; no per-thread mute in this doc.
options.think: a member who follows one thread closely loses it until they unmute the whole channel.
options.then: the agent adds an acceptance row to §6 (AT-4: a thread reply in a muted channel sends nothing), cites the thread send path in §5, and moves the question to §8 as a decision.

options.label: Threads keep notifying; thread muting is a later doc
options.because: the doc as written: it ships without thread-level muting.
options.commits: a follow-up doc for thread muting, and a narrower signal in §0.
options.think: the signal fails for any channel with active threads, so §0 needs your edit before the doc can move on.
options.then: the agent opens a thread-muting doc as a thin draft and shows you the §0 line the signal would need.

items.text: Approve the settings copy for the mute toggle
items.why: The toggle is the only place a member learns what muting does. The doc's first rule (no push and no badge from a muted channel) means the copy has to say both.
items.blocks: The settings screen in build phase 1.
items.ifNoAnswer: Phase 1 ships with the old label, which says nothing about badges.

evidence.note: rule 1: no push or badge count until unmuted

items.code:
- Turn off notifications
+ Mute channel
+ You won't get pushes or badges from this channel until you unmute it.

items.text: How many channels may one member mute?
items.why: The send path reads the mute table before every notification. With no limit, one member with thousands of muted channels makes every send slower for everyone.
items.blocks: The schema in build phase 1 (the index on the mute table).
items.ifNoAnswer: No limit is set; the agent flags it as UNENFORCED in §4.
items.example: Ben is in 800 channels and mutes 600 of them. At 500 he is told he has reached the limit and must unmute one first.

evidence.note: the send path checks the mute table before writing a notification

items.text: Turn the mute flag on in staging
items.why: The red tests in phase 1 run against staging, and they fail for the wrong reason while the flag is off.
items.blocks: Arming the doc: the red gate commit needs staging with the flag on.
items.ifNoAnswer: The agent waits. It cannot turn the flag on: that needs your staging credentials.
